From Ottoman Turkish تازه (tâze), from Persian تازه (tâze).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish دانه (tane), from Persian دانه (dâne).
From Ottoman Turkish تخت (taht), from Persian تخت (taxt).
From Ottoman Turkish تخته (tahta), from Persian تخته (taxte).
From Ottoman Turkish تاج (tac), from Persian تاج (tâj, “crown”).
From Ottoman Turkish تزگاه (tezgâh), from Persian دستگاه (dastgâh).
From Ottoman Turkish ترازو (modern Turkish terazi), from Persian ترازو (tarâzu).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish ترزی (terzi), from Persian درزی (darzi).

parole.significato: plectrum (small piece of plastic, metal, ivory etc. for plucking the strings of a guitar, lyre, mandolin etc.)
parole.testo: From a spoken form of Ottoman Turkish تازیانه (taziyane), from Persian تازیانه (tâziyâna), تارزنه (târzana, “scourge, lash, whip”).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish دستره (destere, testere), from Persian دستره (dastare, “handsaw”), from دست (dast, “hand”) + اره (arre, “saw”).

Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خزنهدار (haznadar), from خزنه (hazna), خزینه (hazine, “treasury”) (Turkish hazne, hazine) + Persian ـدار (-dâr), present stem of داشتن (dâštan, “to have”). Akin to ха̏зна (“treasury”).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خان (han), from Persian خانه (xâne, “house”).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خنجر (hancer), خنچار (hançar) (Turkish hançer), from Persian خنجر (xanjar).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish هفته (hafta), from Persian هفته (hafte, “week”), from هفت (haft, “seven”). Akin to хефта̀лук.
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خروس (horoz), from Persian خروس (xorus).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish خشم (hışım), from Persian خشم (xešm).
From Ottoman Turkish حوری (huri) (Turkish huri), from Persian حوری (huri), from Arabic حُور (ḥūr).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چقال (çakal), from Persian شغال (šaġâl), from Sanskrit सृगाल (sṛgāla, “jackal”). Doublet of ша̏кал, from German Schakal.
From Ottoman Turkish چوراب (çorap), from Persian جوراب (jurâb).
From Ottoman Turkish چارشی (çarşı), from Persian چارسو (čârsu).
From Ottoman Turkish چشمه (çeşma, çeşme), from Persian چشمه (češme).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چراغ (çirâg, çerâg), from Persian چراغ (čerâġ, “lamp, light, wick”).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چراق (çırak), from Persian چراغ (čerâġ). Akin to чира̀клук.
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چوربا (çorba), from Persian شوربا (šurbâ).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish شالوار (şalvâr), from Persian شلوار (šalvâr).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish شاهین (şahin), from Persian شاهین (šâhin), from Middle Persian. Akin to Ша́хин and шахѝнџија.
From Ottoman Turkish شاگرد (şâgird), from Persian شاگرد (šâgerd, “pupil”), from older *Middle Persian ašākert, the later attested form of which is 𐭠𐭱𐭠𐭢𐭥𐭲 (ašāgart).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish شهر (şehir), from Persian شهر (šahr). Akin to Шехе́рија, шехѐрли.

parole.significato: necklace (especially as a part of national costume)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish گردان (gerdan) (Turkish gerdan (“neck”)), from Persian گردن (gardan).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish گردك (Turkish gerdek), from Persian گردک (gerdak).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish گناه (günâh) (Turkish günah), from Persian گناه (gonâh).
Probably from ахар, from Ottoman Turkish آخور (modern Turkish ahır), from Persian آخور (“stable”).
Ottoman Turkish ارغوانی (ergavani, erguvani), from Persian ارغوانی (arġavâni, “purple”). Compare jȍrgovān, adžùvān.
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كار (ḱar), from Persian کار (kâr).
From Ottoman Turkish كبه (kebe), from Persian قبا (qabâ, “garment”), from Arabic قَبَاء (qabāʔ).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كل (kel) (Turkish kel), from Persian کل (kal, “bald”).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كپچه (kepçe), from Persian کپچه (kapče), کفچه (kafče).
From Ottoman Turkish كار (kȃr), from Persian کار (kâr). Compare ћар.
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كهلبار (kehlübar, kehlibar), from Persian کهربا (kahrobâ).

parole.significato: thick carpet or tapestry of oriental style
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كلیم (Turkish kilim), from Persian گلیم (gelim).
From Ottoman Turkish كور (kör), from Persian کور (kur).
From Ottoman Turkish كوسه (köse), from Persian کوسه (kuse, “shark”).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كوشه (köşe), from Persian گوشه (guše).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish كوفته (köfte), from Persian کوفته (kufte), from کوفتن (kuftan, “to grind, break, beat”).
From Ottoman Turkish جان (can), from Persian جان (jân).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish جنازه (cenâze, cinâze), from Persian جنازه (janâze, jenâze), from Arabic جَنَازَة (janāza).
From Ottoman Turkish جكر (Turkish ciğer) + -ица. Further from Persian جگر (jegar), from Proto-Indo-European *Hyékʷr̥ (“liver”), compare Latin iecur.
